# 1 Enoch Chapter 75 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all verses in 1 Enoch Chapter 75 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 75:1 — 'intercalary days' vs. 'extra days' vs. 'days outside the count'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "four-intercalary-days" | Technical term; days inserted to complete the calendar |
| LOGOS | "four intercalary days" | Retains technical term |
| PNEUMA | "four extra days" | More accessible; loses the technical calendrical meaning |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted 'four intercalary days' (EMET/LOGOS). 'Intercalary' is the correct technical calendrical term for days added to complete a schematic year. These four days are placed at the four seasonal transitions (solstices/equinoxes) in the 364-day calendar. Losing this term obscures the calendrical precision the text intends.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS. Technical precision required.

---

## 75:3 — 'Lord of glory' for the divine title

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-Lord-of-glory" | Literal Ge'ez construct; 'glory' = Ge'ez kebr |
| LOGOS | "the Lord of glory" | Retains traditional title |
| PNEUMA | "the Lord of glory" | All three agree |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** All three converge on 'Lord of glory.' This is the standard title for God in 1 Enoch (also appearing in the Similitudes).

**Status:** Converged.

---

## 75:2 — 'go wrong' vs. 'err' vs. 'make errors'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "men-go-wrong therein" | The intercalary days cause human calendrical error |
| LOGOS | "people go wrong therein" | 'People' is more inclusive than 'men' |
| PNEUMA | "people make errors in their reckoning" | Explicates the nature of the error |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted 'people go wrong therein' (LOGOS). 'People' is appropriate; 'go wrong' preserves the moral/navigational metaphor implicit in the Ge'ez. PNEUMA's 'make errors in their reckoning' is explanatory but not wrong — excluded from consensus to keep translation from becoming a commentary.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---
